traps.why: An acid chloride makes the aryl ESTER. For the ether the phenoxide must attack an alkyl halide.
That is Friedel–Crafts C-acylation (a hydroxyaryl ketone). The ether comes from phenoxide + alkyl halide.
Step 1 (CH₃I) does nothing here: A neutral phenol does not attack an alkyl halide; make the phenoxide first (NaOH or K₂CO₃).
Step 1 (NaHCO₃) does nothing here: A phenol (pKa ≈ 10) is not deprotonated by bicarbonate; NaOH does it. (Only picric-acid-like phenols with two o/p nitro groups react.)

explanation: NaOH (or K₂CO₃) deprotonates the phenol; the phenoxide does SN2 on the CH₃/1° halide. The ring brings the oxygen.
tip: Phenol + base + RX = aryl alkyl ether. The O comes from the phenol.
